workflow.contradiction.committedNeedsFol: “Committed is done” needs everyone in the project folder.
workflow.contradiction.hiveMergesNeedsGi: Merging needs Git: without version control, work is accepted where it is.
workflow.contradiction.mergeNeedsSlots: When Hive or the agent merges, each card needs its own folder.
workflow.contradiction.noneHasNoSlots: Without version control, everyone works in the project folder.
workflow.contradiction.okWithReview: Your OK before merging is already part of review by you.
workflow.contradiction.quorumNeedsAgent: Two reviewers per card need review by reviewer agents.
workflow.contradiction.selfReview: “Nobody reviews their own work” can't be off while a reviewer agent checks the work.
workflow.forYou.decidedAfterMerge: {card} was decided after it merged: does it need a follow-up?
workflow.forYou.lineAsk: {line} still has {card}'s work, squashed into {target}: approve and Hive brings the branch up to date once, or decline and do it yourself before {next} starts.
workflow.forYou.lineRefused: Git wouldn't bring {line} up to date with {target}: {reason}. {next} starts once the branch is up to date.
workflow.forYou.lineUnfinished: Hive's move of {line} to {to} didn't finish and couldn't be put back. Bring the branch to {target} with its files and index clean, or back where it was: {next} starts once it is settled.
workflow.forYou.lineWork: {line} has work that isn't in {target}: {commits}. Decide what happens to it: {next} starts once the branch is up to date.
workflow.forYou.newDecision: {card} has a new decision: your review again?
workflow.forYou.queueAdvance: {card} is tested and ready to merge: update {target} in {folder} now?
workflow.forYou.queueStuck: {card}'s merge into {target} stopped part way in {folder}, with {files, plural, one {# file} other {# files}} left between the two, and Hive changes nothing more there. The card's Work section lists each file and its side, and the commands to copy. {how, select, both {To finish it, run {finish} (PowerShell) in {project}; to undo it, run {undo} (PowerShell) in {folder}.} finish {To finish it, run {finish} (PowerShell) in {folder}.} undo {To undo it, run {undo} (PowerShell) in {folder}.} other {Its files are neither as they were nor as merged: put them right by hand.}} Then answer here, and the queue looks again.
workflow.forYou.roundLimit: {card} failed {rounds, plural, one {# review} other {# reviews}}: carry on with more rounds, split it, accept it with follow-ups, or take it over?
workflow.forYouKind: {kind, select, approve {Approve} decide {Decide} test {Test} signIn {Sign in} other {Other}}

workflow.form.fileLocksValue: As set for the project’s agents
workflow.form.folders: Folders and files, separated by commas

workflow.form.invalid: These options can’t be used, so every rule is off in this project:

workflow.form.loopsValue: {rounds, plural, one {# round} other {# rounds}}, wait {hours, plural, one {# hour} other {# hours}}
workflow.form.noChanges: No option changes: only the preset they started from.
workflow.form.noIdentity: No name and email are set in git config yet.
workflow.form.notEnforced: Workflow rules aren’t enforced (Settings → Advanced). These options are saved, and apply once the rules are enforced again.
workflow.form.pasteBad: That isn’t workflow options copied from Hive.
workflow.form.pasteMessage: Paste options copied from a project with the same version control. They replace the form’s, to save afterwards.
workflow.form.pastePlatform: These options are for another version control.
workflow.form.platformDesc: Found in the project folder. The options below are this version control’s.
workflow.form.presetDesc: Fills in every option at once. Changing an option afterwards makes it Custom.
workflow.form.worktree: In this version, a card’s own folder is its builder’s worktree.
workflow.notOffered.hiveMerges: “Hive merges” isn’t available in this version yet: choose “The agent merges, Hive checks”.
workflow.notOffered.later: Some of these options aren’t available in this version yet: leave them as they are.
workflow.option.commands.desc: The command each named check runs. A run counts as the check only when it runs that command.
workflow.option.commands.title: Check commands
workflow.option.dependenciesDone.desc: A card that waits for others can’t start before their work is in.
workflow.option.dependenciesDone.none: Cards start only when the cards they wait for are done
workflow.option.dependenciesDone.title: Cards start only when the cards they wait for are merged
workflow.option.excluded.desc: The whole project folder, apart from these folders and files (.hive always).
workflow.option.excluded.title: What the work is
workflow.option.finish.desc: When a card is done: once Hive’s merge queue has merged it, once its agent has merged it and Hive finds the work in the target branch, once it is committed, or whenever it is moved there.
workflow.option.finish.title: Who merges
workflow.option.folder.desc: In its own folder, a card is built in its builder’s worktree, apart from other agents’ work. In the project folder, everyone sees each other’s unfinished changes.
workflow.option.folder.title: Where cards are built
workflow.option.identity.desc: Commits are made with the name and email from the project’s git config (else your global one).
workflow.option.identity.title: Commits use the project’s identity
workflow.option.mergeChecks.desc: Each check is a named command. Hive’s merge queue runs them on the card’s work merged with the target branch, and moves the target only once each one has passed.
workflow.option.mergeChecks.title: Checks pass on the merged result
workflow.option.mergeInstall.desc: Before the checks on the merged result. A change to the lock file or the manifests always installs from scratch, whichever you choose.
workflow.option.mergeInstall.title: Install dependencies from scratch
workflow.option.noSelfReview.desc: Always on while a reviewer agent checks the work.
workflow.option.noSelfReview.title: Nobody reviews their own work
workflow.option.okBefore.desc: A card waits for your OK before it is merged: never, only cards with these labels, or every card.
workflow.option.okBefore.title: Your OK before merging
workflow.option.preChecks.desc: Each check is a named command. A card goes to review only once each one has passed on its work.
workflow.option.preChecks.title: Checks pass before review
workflow.option.review.desc: A card goes to Review when its builder submits it, and on once it passes. With you as well, it waits for your OK after the reviewer.
workflow.option.review.none: Who checks the work before it’s done
workflow.option.review.title: Work is reviewed before it’s merged
workflow.option.reviewers.desc: With two, both must pass the same change.
workflow.option.reviewers.title: Reviewers per card
workflow.option.sameness.desc: With the same change, a pass still counts after the work is moved onto newer commits without changing it.
workflow.option.sameness.title: A pass survives a clean rebase
workflow.option.sharedFolderWarning.desc: In the project folder, a submit warns when its commit takes in files another agent is editing. It never refuses.
workflow.option.sharedFolderWarning.titl: Warn when a commit includes another agent’s files
workflow.option.stopOwnRuns.desc: A card goes to review only once its builder’s own runs and background commands have stopped.
workflow.option.stopOwnRuns.title: Agents stop what they started before review
workflow.option.strict.desc: When the target branch has moved on since the review, Hive’s merge queue merges it into the card’s work (or rebases the work, with the Squash merge style) in its own folder, never on the builder’s branch. The review still counts if the result is the same change; if not, or if it conflicts, the card goes back to its builder.
workflow.option.strict.title: Work is up to date with its target branch before it merges
workflow.option.style.desc: How a card’s work is merged into the target branch.
workflow.option.style.title: Merge style
workflow.option.target.desc: The target branch. Left empty, the repository’s default branch.
workflow.option.target.title: Work merges into
workflow.preset.needs.hiveMerges: Needs Hive to merge cards, which comes in a later version.
workflow.preset.needs.slots: Needs a folder of its own for every card, which comes in a later version.
workflow.preset.note.team: Team checks the merged result with the quick checks and the unit tests. Running each card’s own focused tests there too comes in a later version.
workflow.presetsNotice.text: {n, plural, one {{projects} works} other {{projects} work}} as before this version. A preset sets up a workflow in one click: who reviews the work, which checks pass first and who merges.

workflow.refused.done.contained.change: This rule is set in Version Control → Who merges.

workflow.refused.evidence.changed.messag: What Hive read for {card} changed while it decided.

workflow.refused.lane.oneAtATime.message: {card} can't start yet: {earlier}, before it in its lane, isn't Done.
workflow.refused.lane.oneAtATime.next: Finish {earlier} first: once it is Done, the lane goes on to {card}.
workflow.refused.loop.roundLimit.message: {card} reached its round limit: it goes on once its round-limit question is answered.
workflow.refused.loop.roundLimit.next: The question is on the card (For you): once it is answered, Hive wakes the agents waiting on it.
workflow.refused.merge.hiveMerges.change: This rule is set in Version Control → Who merges. A card keeps the rules it started with.
workflow.refused.merge.hiveMerges.messag: Hive merges {card}: agents don't merge it or report its merge.
workflow.refused.merge.hiveMerges.next: Once it is approved, the merge queue merges it and moves it to Done: wait for that, or for it to come back.
workflow.refused.merge.hiveMerges.nextMe: The merge queue has merged it already: nothing is left to do.
workflow.refused.merge.hiveMerges.nextPa: It is in the merge queue for {target}, which is paused until it is resumed: wait for Done, or for it to come back.
It is in the merge queue for {target}, which is paused until the user answers in For you: wait for Done, or for it to come back.
It is in the merge queue for {target}, which is paused until the user fixes what stopped it and resumes it: wait for Done, or for it to come back.
It is in the merge queue for {target}, which is paused until the user puts right the folder {target} is checked out in and resumes it: wait for Done, or for it to come back.

It is in the merge queue for {target}, which paused while workflow rules were off and moves on once they are enforced again (if they already are, once the user resumes it): wait for Done, or for it to come back.

workflow.refused.merge.hiveMerges.nextRe: It came back from the merge queue: fix it in your worktree, commit and submit again.
workflow.refused.merge.hiveMerges.nextTe: The merge queue is merging it into {target} now and moves it to Done once merged: wait for that, or for it to come back.
workflow.refused.move.needsOverride.chan: These rules are set in Version Control, where the user can change them.
